simple.meaning: פָּשַׁט (pâshaṭ) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to spread out (i.e. deploy in hostile array); by analogy, to strip (i.e. unclothe, plunder, flay, etc.).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 43 times across Genesis, Leviticus, Numbers, Judges, 1 Samuel, and 11 more, beginning at Genesis 37:23. Its contexts include family, family line, offering, death, mountain.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to פָּשַׁט (H6584).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: פָּשַׁט (pâshaṭ) / H6584 is traced through Genesis 37:23, Leviticus 1:6, Leviticus 6:4, Leviticus 16:23 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.short: to spread out (i.e. deploy in hostile array); by analogy, to strip (i.e. unclothe, plunder, flay, etc.)
definitions.usage: fall upon, flay, invade, make an invasion, pull off, put off, make a road, run upon, rush, set, spoil, spread selves (abroad), strip (off, self).
